title: IPO Report Card: 30 to 60 Days After Listing — September 2026
description: Out of 40 IPOs that listed between 30 and 60 days ago, 27 companies are currently trading above their initial issue price. 13 companies are currently trading .

faq.a: An IPO (Initial Public Offering) is when a private company first offers its shares to the public to raise money, allowing ordinary investors to buy a part of the company.
A Mainboard IPO is for larger, more established companies that list their shares on the main exchanges like the National Stock Exchange (NSE) or Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
An SME (Small and Medium Enterprise) IPO is for smaller companies that list on dedicated platforms within the NSE or BSE, often with different rules and lower minimum investment amounts.
The issue price is the fixed price per share at which the company offers its shares to investors during the IPO.
Listing gain is the percentage difference between the IPO issue price and the price at which the shares close on their first day of trading on the stock exchange.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of IPO performance and related concepts, with most factual claims aligning with regulatory information. However, there is a minor inaccuracy regarding the anchor investor lock-in period.

corrections.note: Corrected the lock-in period for anchor investors based on SEBI guidelines.

edits.why: SEBI guidelines state that 50% of anchor investor shares are locked in for 90 days and the remaining 50% for 30 days, not all for 30 days.
